thread.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq Pile On Records As Mastecard, Adobe Hit Buy Points

author: JUAN CARLOS ARANCIBIA
title: S&P 500, Nasdaq Pile On Records As Mastecard, Adobe Hit Buy Points
text:
The Nasdaq composite and the S&P 500 today made new highs once again, while some top-rated stocks broke out and Morgan Stanley struck a bullish tone on market leaders Alphabet ( GOOGL ) and Amazon.com ( AMZN ).
X The Nasdaq added 0.9% for its third consecutive new high. The S&P 500 climbed 0.6% as it set course for a fourth straight advance. Indexes stopped climbing about 11:30 a.m. ET but were holding near session highs.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose a more modest 0.3%. Tech components Microsoft ( MSFT ), Cisco Systems ( CSCO ) and Apple ( AAPL ) made new highs. Visa ( V ) also made an all-time high.
The Russell 2000 rose 0.4%, and the small-cap index remained in a moderate uptrend.

Apple and Microsoft's gains gave the Nasdaq an edge. Other major techs also performed well as Morgan Stanley gave bullish comments on Alphabet and Amazon.com.
Alphabet rose 1.3% after a Morgan Stanley analyst raised his price target to 1,515 from 1,325 and kept an overweight rating. The analyst lauded Alphabet's Waymo self-driving taxi business. Morgan Stanley says the parent company of Google is on a path toward $1 trillion in market cap.
Morgan Stanley also raised the price target on Amazon to 2,500, from 1,850. Amazon is now trading around 1,982, up 2.6% on the day. The firm reiterated an overweight rating. Shares rallied 3%.
Several leading stocks broke out of bases, with varying degrees of strength.
Vertex Pharmaceuticals ( VRTX ) cleared a flat base but volume was not even at the average pace. PayPal ( PYPL ) also topped a flat base but volume was unimpressive. Jefferies raised its price target on PayPal shares to 110 from 100.
Mastercard ( MA ) broke out of a flat base with a 214.38 buy point. Adobe Systems ( ADBE ) climbed past the 263.93 entry of a flat base in volume 30% higher than usual.
Leading stocks in general were positive, with the IBD 50 up 0.8%. Health care and software companies led the IBD 50 today.
The energy sector resumed its rebound after a one-day drop. Oil prices rose 1.1% $69.32 a barrel. Weekly data showed a drop in U.S. oil stockpiles , while signs emerged that Iran's August exports likely fell ahead of U.S. sanctions.
